title: HuPER: A Human-Inspired Framework for Phonetic Perception
claim: Our method reaches lower error than prior systems while using orders of magnitude less training data.
layout: 1 scatter plot, log-x training data vs error, two legends
description: A single scatter plot. The x-axis is training data in hours on a log scale, from about 10^2 to 10^4. The y-axis is error, where lower is better, from about 8 to 25. Marker shape identifies the model: circle, square, triangle, inverted triangle, diamond, plus, X and star. The star is HuPER (ours). Marker color identifies the benchmark: blue, orange, green, red or purple. A shape legend sits in the upper left and a color legend in the upper right. Baseline markers sit at 2,000 to 30,000 hours and span errors of about 10 to 25. Five star markers sit alone in the lower-left corner at about 100 hours with errors of about 7 to 11. The eye goes first to this isolated cluster of stars.
caption: HuPER achieves highly data-efficient phonetic transcription on English variation benchmarks.
abstract: We propose HuPER, a human-inspired framework that models phonetic perception as adaptive inference over acoustic-phonetics evidence and linguistic knowledge. With only 100 hours of training data, HuPER achieves state-of-the-art phonetic error rates on five English benchmarks and strong zero-shot transfer to 95 unseen languages. HuPER is also the first framework to enable adaptive, multi-path phonetic perception under diverse acoustic conditions. All training data, models, and code are open-sourced. Code and demo avaliable at https://github.com/Berkeley-Speech-Group/HuPER.
